premises.statement: The data-quality assessment may assign consistency, accuracy, and overall quality scores of 85 and fixed classifications and recommendations without computing them from source data.
premises.evidence_of_dependence: 85::DOUBLE consistency_score,85::DOUBLE accuracy_score,85::DOUBLE overall_quality_score,'Good'::VARCHAR quality_grade,'No Major Issues'::VARCHAR primary_concern
premises.alternative: The contract requires consistency from integrity percentages, accuracy from business-rule compliance, and overall quality from the three component scores; it also requires 'Maintain Current Data Quality Standards' when the overall score is at least 85.
premises.reason: The revised model substitutes constants for the assessment's principal measurements and decision outputs.

premises.statement: The completeness score may always be 85 without evaluating transaction and customer missing-value counts.
premises.alternative: The contract requires averaging table-specific completeness scores: transactions and customers receive 100 or 70 according to their specified null counts, while transaction lines receive 85.
premises.reason: The replacement removes all source-dependent completeness evaluation rather than merely omitting the customer-name check.
